rows: What is the single most impactful tillage change?
Switch from moldboard plow to no-till or strip-till; eliminates annual SOM oxidation flush and residue burial; C benefits compound over 5–15 yr
Which cover crop best protects against N leaching?
Cereal rye (winter-hardy, grows at 4°C, absorbs 50–90 kg N/ha); best catch crop in cold climates
Which cover crop provides N to the next cash crop?
Hairy vetch or crimson clover (50–200 kg N/ha fixed); terminate while actively growing (C:N < 20) for fast N release
How long to detect soil carbon gains from no-till?
SOC change detectable in 5–10 yr; active C (POXC, CO2 burst) changes in 1–3 yr; use early indicators for progress tracking
Degraded tropical acid soils (Oxisols) and sandy soils needing pH correction and water retention; negligible effect in well-managed temperate soils
Right Source × Right Rate × Right Time × Right Place for nutrient application; framework for simultaneously maximizing efficiency and minimizing environmental loss
Is agricultural soil carbon sequestration a viable climate solution?

Partial mitigation (1–3 Pg C/yr potential globally); not a silver bullet; permanence and measurement remain unsolved problems; practice-based payments more reliable than voluntary carbon markets currently
